title: You can look holy… and still be completely fake.
paragraphs: You can look holy… and still be completely fake.
You lift your hands at the right moment.
And you’re hoping no one notices.

What if your devotion is real on the outside…
but counterfeit in the eyes of God?
What if the mask has become your identity?
What if you’ve learned how to perform Christianity…
but never actually surrendered to Christ?
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable.
You can do all of that…
“Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of My Father who is in heaven.” — Matthew 7:21
Jesus is not impressed with words.
Some scholars interpret this passage as a direct warning against false assurance—people who genuinely believe they are saved, but have never truly submitted their lives to Christ.
Because if we’re real for a moment—
We’ve all tried to manage sin instead of killing it.
That private life that doesn’t match your public faith.
Here’s the truth we don’t like to say out loud:

Counterfeit faith doesn’t reject Jesus outright…
it resists His authority quietly.
But Scripture cuts through the noise:
“Examine yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith. Test yourselves.” — 2 Corinthians 13:5
Because God is not trying to expose you to shame you.
He’s exposing you to save you.
Now here comes the turning point.
Jesus did not come for the polished.
He did not die for the image you project.
He died for the sin you hide.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Not when you cleaned up your act.
While you were still in it.
Every moment you chose yourself over Him.
You are more sinful than you admit…
but more loved than you can comprehend—
“For the grace of God has appeared… training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives.”
So if your version of Christianity never challenges your sin…
You don’t have to stay there.
You don’t have to keep pretending.
You don’t have to keep performing.
You don’t have to keep living divided.
“Jesus, I don’t want a fake faith anymore. Expose what’s false in me. Break what needs breaking. Lead me into truth.”
And when you come to Him—
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
